Design and Image Credits

Design foundation

Adapted from Glenn Sorrentino’s design system, using its reset, typography, font assets, and theme foundations. Atkinson Hyperlegible by the Braille Institute; IBM Plex Mono by IBM.

From the Field Station dataset.

The featured images are actual human-reviewed observation crops classified as anomalous by human reviewers. They are the existing review images, used without generative edits. In the intro, a detection is composited over a separate Milky Way photograph using screen blending; this is a design composite, not a single observation of that sky. The flow diagram shows the unblended review crops. An anomalous label records a review decision, not an identification or explanation. The yellow frame encloses the reviewed crop.

Milky Way background

Milkyway nightsky longexposure photography (1) 01 by Nikhil More, via Wikimedia Commons. Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. Displayed with a responsive crop, a dark gradient, and a separately captured detection overlay. The adapted intro composition is also available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

Stars 01 (MK) by Mathias Krumbholz, licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0. Cropped and clipped to the heading lettering; this heading adaptation is distributed under the same license.

Archive video excerpt

The archive preview is a silent 6.9-second excerpt from review fbd7ff04bb6a76a209167eb5b3ad8171, starting at 3.005 seconds. A fixed 480 × 360-pixel crop shows the upper-right region, scaled to 720 × 540 for display. A fixed-size yellow box follows interpolated human-review centers and appears only during bright flashes measured in the clip. Original playback speed and color are retained; no generated detail is added. View its full archive bundle.

Star People identity

The mark represents four observers sharing one star. Concept exploration used image generation; the final artwork is constructed SVG. The outlined wordmark is derived from the regular and bold Atkinson Hyperlegible letterforms by Braille Institute of America, with a custom weight and optical spacing. The site continues to use the original Atkinson fonts.
